stories.title: MHRA approves zanidatamab (Ziihera) for the treatment of gastroesophageal cancer
stories.summary: Zanidatamab was previously approved for the treatment of adults with bile duct cancer. Zanidatamab is used when the cancer cannot be removed by surgery and has spread to nearby tissues or other parts of the body. It is used alongside chemotherapy, with or without another cancer medicine called tislelizumab, depending on the level of HER2 in the cancer. Zanidatamab is administered by an infusion drip into a vein every two or three weeks. In a study of 914 patients with HER2-positive gastroesophageal cancer, patients who received zanidatamab alongside chemotherapy and tislelizumab lived on average around seven months longer, and around four months longer without their cancer getting worse. “This approval provides a new treatment option for adults with HER2-positive gastroesophageal cancer, where the cancer cannot be removed by surgery or has spread to other parts of the body. “This approval reflects the MHRA’s commitment to ensuring patients can access safe and effective medicines where there is an unmet clinical need.

stories.title: Cape Hatteras National Seashore Provides Updates Following Coastal Storm Impacts
stories.summary: News Release Date: November 27, 2026 Contact: Cape Hatteras Public Affairs MANTEO, N.C. — National Park Service staff continue to assess damage and public safety conditions across Cape Hatteras National Seashore following a significant coastal storm that caused erosion, roadway damage and impacts to visitor facilities. Road Closures Three sections of N.C. Highway 12 remain closed by the N.C. Department of Transportation as recovery efforts continue. Closures are in effect between Oregon Inlet and Rodanthe, between the villages of Frisco and Hatteras, and near the north end of Ocracoke Island. Travelers should expect delays and monitor drivenc.gov for updates. Storm Impacts On Hatteras and Ocracoke islands, thousands of feet of dunes were lost due to erosion and multiple sections of N.C. Highway 12 sustained damage, leading to the closures. The Avon Fishing Pier also sustained storm damage. Seashore staff are coordinating with the pier leaseholder to evaluate damages and determine repair plans.

stories.title: Huge trade boost for Northern Ireland as UK-EU trade deal tears down 90% of checks on goods from Great Britain
stories.summary: The agreement, struck by the PM in Brussels last week, will help to keep costs down and improve customer choice across the UK, Biosecurity and Trade Minister Baroness Hayman said today (Friday 27 November). Baroness Hayman visited Creative Gardens in Donaghadee, Lidl in Belfast, and farmers in Kilbride, and met CBI business leaders to see how the new UK-EU deal will cut checks and paperwork for local firms. She also met Northern Ireland Executive Minister for agriculture, Andrew Muir, to discuss the positive impacts of the deal and the benefits to food businesses and farmers. Analysis suggests sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) checks on vehicles moving goods from Great Britain to Northern Ireland could fall by up to 90% once the new arrangements are fully in place.
stories.why_it_matters: Understanding money and business can help us make sense of everyday decisions.

stories.title: Mini lab-grown human organs to boost search for new treatments as £20m Cambridge lab opens
stories.summary: As the £20 million UK Preclinical Translational Models Hub opens its doors, the laboratory will help to usher in a world of new possibilities for patients. Faster access to treatments, a better understanding of how medicines behave inside the body, and fewer animal experiments will all be supported through a new lab opening in Cambridge today (27 November). The site will use organoids - tiny versions of human organs made from tissue donated by NHS patients - to help researchers build up a more accurate picture of the most promising new drugs to take forward for clinical trials. Some studies show that lab-grown organs could actually reduce total pharmaceutical R&D costs by between 10% to 26% . It also has the potential to slash the time it takes for the most promising drugs to move into full scale development by nearly a fifth – meaning a quicker route to get cutting-edge treatments into the hands of health workers.
